column1: Unit 1: Organisation of Production and Rural Economy

column3: Purpose of Production: To produce goods and services that people need
Factors of Production

column4: Land: Natural resources such as land, water, forests, and minerals
Labour: People who work, from skilled professionals to manual workers

column5: Fixed Capital: Tools, machines, and buildings used repeatedly
Working Capital: Raw materials and money used during production

column4: Human Capital: Knowledge and enterprise that organise production

column3: Land Constraints: Cultivable land is fixed and limited
Multiple Cropping: Growing more than one crop on the same land in a year
Modern Farming Methods

column4: Green Revolution: Introduced HYV seeds in the late 1960s
Input Requirements: Fertilisers, pesticides, and assured irrigation

column3: Environmental Impact

column4: Soil Fertility Loss: Overuse of chemical inputs reduces soil quality
Groundwater Depletion: Excessive irrigation lowers water table

column3: Dairy: Selling milk
Small-Scale Manufacturing: Production using simple tools at home
Shopkeeping: Trading goods brought from towns
Transport Services: Vehicles used to transport people and goods

column1: Unit 2: People as Resource and Human Capital

column3: Population as Asset: Becomes productive with education and healthcare
Return on Investment: Higher productivity and higher income
Primary Sector: Agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining, animal husbandry
Secondary Sector: Manufacturing activities
Tertiary Sector: Services like transport, banking, health, education
Seasonal Unemployment: Lack of work during certain months of the year
Disguised Unemployment: More workers employed than required
Educated Unemployment: Educated people unable to find suitable jobs
Multi-Dimensional Nature: Hunger, shelterlessness, job insecurity, helplessness
Measurement Basis: Income or consumption level
Calorie Norms

column4: Rural Areas: 2400 calories per person per day
Urban Areas: 2100 calories per person per day

column3: Authority: NITI Aayog
Indicators: Health, education, and standard of living
Social Exclusion: Poor denied access to basic facilities
Vulnerability: Higher risk of poverty among certain social groups
Growth-Oriented Strategy: Economic growth to raise incomes

column4: MGNREGA (2005): Provides 100 days of guaranteed wage employment

Affordability: People can buy nutritious food
